leo: Morning — stopped by Midtown Immediate Care and they said they couldn't verify my insurance so they made me pay $120 up front. I only had the digital ID in the insurer app. What should I do to get reimbursed?

marta (People Ops): Sorry that happened, @leo. Quick steps: (1) get an itemized receipt (must show date, service line, total, provider name), (2) download the insurer digital ID PDF, (3) submit an out-of-pocket claim to the insurer and cc benefits@redwood.com.

leo: The receipt is just a total and the clinic's phone. They said they don't include CPTs unless requested.

broker-amy: Call the clinic billing line and ask for an "itemized statement" or UB-04. Also request their NPI or tax ID — that helps the insurer. If they refuse, the receipt plus a short clinic note often works.

claims-bot: Digital ID available: https://portal.insurer/ids/leo-556677.pdf (expires 2027-02-01)

marta (People Ops): Template you can use to email claims:
```
To: claims@insurer.example
Subject: Member claim submission  urgent care 2026-11-05  Member ID: 556677
Body: Please find attached an itemized receipt for urgent care on 2026-11-05 for Leo K. Provider: Midtown Immediate Care. Member ID: 556677, Group: RW-00011. Please process for reimbursement or advise next steps.
Attachments: itemized_receipt.pdf, digital_id.pdf
```

leo: Sent the insurer the receipt and cc'd benefits. If insurer denies because the provider wasn't in the directory, can we open a provider-directory dispute?

broker-amy: Yes. If provider is actually in-network, we can file a directory dispute and request reprocessing. We'll coordinate once benefits@redwood.com confirms.

marta (People Ops): Thanks @leo, we'll monitor. Typical timeline: insurer ack 3-7 business days, EOB 2-4 weeks. If you get denied, forward the EOB and we'll help file an appeal.

leo: Great — appreciate the help. I'll update when they respond.
